newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: European Union and South Korea sign trade pact.
newsitem.headline: European Union and South Korea sign trade pact.

text.p: South Korea and the European Union on Monday put simmering trade differences on the backburner and signed a lucrative five-year agreement to boost political and economic links.
Under the agreement both sides will grant each other most-favoured nation trading status as well as develop commercial, scientific and technology links.
Korean Foreign Minister Gong Ro-Myung signed the agreement with European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, representing the EU's presidency.

All sides, however, were careful to skirt around a row over European access to South Korea's lucrative telecoms market. The Commission -- the EU's executive -- has threatened to escalate the matter at the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
The EU accuses Seoul of loading government telecoms purchases in favour of suppliers from Korea or the United States -- with whom it has a preferential trade agreement.
Brittan said, however, he was happy progress was being made to iron out differences.

"I am very pleased to be able to formalise our relations by signing this agreement today," he said. "It is not just an expression of goodwill, but a combination of economic and political cooperation that will benefit both sides."
Gong said relations with the EU were an important part of Korea's globalisation drive and he also welcomed European participation in the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation (KEDO).
The EU is currently negotiating entry to KEDO, established by Japan, the U.S. and South Korea to help steer North Korea's nuclear energy programme towards peaceful means.
Korea is one of the EU's most significant trade partners accounting for a balance in favour of the 15-nation bloc of some 904 European currency units in the first five months of this year.
